body: We should expand this.  All of tools/build_defs/pkg is python 2-ish. Someone needs to update them all.

Sigh, another case of #4815. The binary declares that it's PY2 but it's ignored at runtime. This would've been fixed in 0.26 by `--incompatible_use_python_toolchains` but we had to delay that flag flip because of downstream failures. You can try enabling that flag in your build or set a `--python_top` to a workaround `py_runtime` target as in [here](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/4815#issuecomment-460777113).

Actually scratch that, this happens when you pass in the flag to change the default Python version as it is known to Bazel at analysis time, so #4815 isn't relevant. This sounds more like it's getting the Python version from the host platform. That's #6443.

The workaround is to opt out of updating the Python version for host-configured targets by passing `--host_force_python=PY2`.

@brandjon thanks for triaging. Does `--host_force_python=PY2` enforce that all `cfg="host"` targets and `genrule`s _must_ use Python 2? Or just that they will by default if the tool itself doesn't declare a `python_version`? In my case we have a bunch of Python-3-only tools, so it won't help to force them all to use Python 2.

It's that they must be PY2. Unfortunately there can only be one "host" configuration so all host-configured targets have to be the same Python version. There's work on the [execution transition](https://github.com/bazelbuild/proposals/blob/master/designs/2019-02-12-execution-transitions.md) to replace the host configuration.

If your build was working prior to turning on `--incompatible_py3_is_default`, then all your host-configured tools were running as PY2. This is the behavior you preserve by using `--host_force_python=PY2`; the incompatible flag changes the default for both the target and host to PY3, and this force flag sets the host back.

Now, it's possible that targets that were configured for one version of Python end up actually running with an interpreter for the other, depending on the values of `--python_top` / `--python_path` (see #4815). It's still the case that only one runtime is used however.

Actually, this issue is preventing my org from even turning on the `--incompatible_allow_python_version_transitions` flag, so we haven't gotten to the point where we can try `--incompatible_py3_is_default` yet (I created this issue when I was doing discovery work for the transition). 

We can currently get away with having both PY2-only and PY3-only host-configured tools in the same workspace because we're using the `py_runtime` shell script hack where we pick a Python interpreter based on the shebang of the script. The `pkg_rpm` rule works because it falls back to Python 2, and all of our tools work because we specify Python 3 in the shebang.

Ultimately our problem is solved if:
1. All rules like `pkg_rpm` that use Python tools add Python 3 support
2. There is true support for having both PY2 and PY3 tools run on the host

Will using `cfg="exec"` (once it's implemented) actually allow for the second option?

Why is `--incompatible_allow_python_version_transitions` causing failures? That shouldn't change the behavior of the host config.

The `py_runtime` shell script hack, since it is an execution-time hack, should continue to work regardless of all these flags. But analysis-time logic, like `srcs_version` attribute validation, is affected.

`cfg="exec"` should in principle allow for (2), but it will require moving dependencies from a host-configured attribute to an "exec"-configured attribute. E.g., `genrule` will get an `exec_tools` attribute that functions like `tools` except for this difference. (It's also possible that the Configurability team will find a way to change all host-configured attributes to exec-configured without the need for new attributes.)

Turning on the flag isn't, by itself, causing issues for us. However, the main reason we want to turn the flag on is to get rid of the runtime hack and start using the `python_version` attribute instead of shebangs. It sounds like until exec-config is implemented we can't really drop the hack.
The issue for exec transition btw is https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/7935, which does seem to be making good progress.

issue.title: Fixed Python 3 incompatibility in make_rpm tool

labels.name: team-Rules-Server
labels.description: Issues for serverside rules included with Bazel

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
This addresses #7914 , i.e. allowing the `pkg_rpm` rule to be used with either a PY2 or PY3 host configuration, by fixing a Python 3 incompatibility in `make_rpm.py`.

I added a test case that ensures the fixed codepath is covered. It effectively fakes out the `rpmbuild` executable with a shell script, so I'm not sure if there will be concerns with cross-platform compatibility. If so, I could create a Python script for this, or I'm open to other suggestions.

body:
@apt-itude  This is now fixed in rules_pkg. Are you able to migrate to that?
https://github.com/bazelbuild/rules_pkg/releases

@aiuto yup! My fix to make `make_rpm` Python-3 compatible actually made it into Bazel before you forked, so we migrated to `rules_pkg` as soon as you made the first release instead of waiting for the Bazel release, and all is well 👍
Yup. It seems fixed in rules pkg, so closing.
